traceability.notes:
Story 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION is fully implemented and verified.
The `valid-story-reference` ESLint rule, together with `storyReferenceUtils` and its helper module, implements all specified requirements: - It parses @story annotations from comments and extracts file paths (REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION). - It resolves paths relative to the project (cwd) and configured `storyDirectories`, including explicit `./` and `../` forms (REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS). - It enforces `.story.md` by default and supports relaxing this via `requireStoryExtension` (extension handling is clearly validated by tests and documented) (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS). - It performs security validations against absolute paths and traversal outside the project, with a dedicated project-boundary layer that ensures no out-of-project file is treated as valid even if it exists (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY). - It uses a cached filesystem existence layer that never throws, distinguishes between missing vs filesystem-error states, and exposes both boolean and rich status APIs (REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING). - Diagnostics for missing files, invalid extensions, invalid paths, and filesystem errors are clear, contextual (include the path and, for FS errors, error details), and are tested explicitly, satisfying the user-experience and error-handling acceptance criteria. - Documentation in docs/rules/valid-story-reference.md explains the behavior, configuration, and boundary semantics aligning with the story’s implementation notes.
All Jest tests, including the suites explicitly tied to this story, pass successfully, providing strong evidence that acceptance criteria and detailed requirements are met. Therefore the status for this story is PASSED.
